reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight is that even a contamination-free holdout fails to eliminate pretraining familiarity effects. The paper demonstrates that models like TimesFM, which were pretrained on Wikipedia pageviews, outperform competitors on similar domains. This suggests that performance gains are not due to generalization but to familiarity with the training domain. The contamination-free protocol ensures no memorization, yet the within-family comparison still shows a significant advantage. This implies that domain familiarity is a persistent trait in TSFM architectures. The mathematical structure of this phenomenon can be modeled as a kernel-based similarity measure in the space of pretraining domains, where the kernel value reflects the degree of overlap between training and test domains. The derived metric 'familiarity gap' quantifies this effect, enabling GSE to distinguish between true generalization and pretraining bias. The failure mode lies in assuming that temporal separation alone suffices to prevent contamination, when in fact domain-specific knowledge persists.
